en: Compiled by the monk Daoxian, a seeker of the Way under Chan Master Dahuipujiao, this is the *Zongmen Wuku* (Armory of the Gate of the School).
The Elder Guang of Dongshan was a native of Zizhou; he was known in the monastic community as Guang Wuxin. Initially, he traveled abroad to seek instruction.
He asked Master Yungai Zhi, "What was the meaning behind Xinghua’s striking of the *weina*?
Zhi descended from his rope seat, extended both hands, and showed his tongue; he then struck out a full sitting mat.
Zhìyún said, "This is turned by the power of the wind.
He then took these words and questioned Master Shīshuāng Lín.
Lín said, "What do you think?
Guǎng also struck his meditation mat once.
Lin said, "What a fine sitting mat!
It is simply that you do not know where its point of rest lies."
He asked Zhenjing again,
"What do you think? Jing replied, "How would you put it?"
Guang also struck his meditation mat once.
Jing said, "He struck it; you strike it too."
Guang attained a great awakening through this.
Zhenjing then composed a verse, saying:
"A man of courage should sever [delusions] himself; he must not fail to sever them."
Xinghua was a man who had reached the ultimate depth.
Later, his own eyes opened by themselves;
he was bound with a staff, fined, and driven out of the monastery.
Ciming, Langlang, Dayu, and several others took their leave of Fenyang;
they vied with one another and were unwilling to serve as the head of the group. Fenyang said:
This matter cannot be judged by the number of years one has maintained the precepts.
Listen to this verse of mine:
"The heavens have no head; at the foot of Mount Jiuzhou, spears and halberds are unfurled."
The General passes through the forest on a single horse;
within the city of Yuanzhou, there is a clamor.
Ciming stepped forward from the ranks and said:
"Chu Yuan, what person would dare to receive such a transmission?
Thereupon, he led the assembly in taking leave.
Master Zhantang Zhun had initially studied under Zhenjing.
Jing asked, "Where did you recently leave?
Cun replied, "Dagyang. Jing asked, "Where were you during the summer retreat?"
Zhun said, "Daguang. Jing said,
"Whose business is this?"
Zhun said: "In Xingyuan Prefecture,
Jingzhan spread both hands and said:"
"What is my hand like compared to the Buddha’s hand?
Zhen was at a loss for words. Jing said:
Just now, when responding to each question, you were one by one luminous, intelligent, and true;
yet as soon as the word "Buddha-hand" was uttered, it became an obstruction.
Tell me, where does the sickness lie?
Zhun said, "I do not understand. Jing said:
All were fully realized; furthermore, he taught only those who had attained assembly.
The Master Xian had long studied under Xuedou;
Xuedou intended to appoint him as the abbot of Jing’e.
Upon hearing this, Xian secretly inscribed a verse on the wall of the abbot’s quarters during the night and then fled.
The verse said:
"It is not that I lack the mind to continue the ancestral lamp."
Daozan has not yet attained the ability of Neng in Lingnan;
at the third watch under the moon, he departs from his mountain cave.
Full of lingering affection, he remains silent as he gazes upon the verdant peaks.
It is further said:
"For more than thirty years throughout the four seas,
I have sought teachers and chosen friends, never once finding leisure."
This morning I attained the state of no-mind;
yet, being pursued by that very no-mind, I left the mountain.
Later, Xian succeeded to the Dharma and opened the Way.
Chengsi succeeded the Venerable Yǎn of Dēngshān and continued the correspondence with Xuědòu.
When the old woman by the mountain front saw the special messenger, she asked him with delight:
When Chan Master Xian was appointed to head a monastery,
he burned incense alone.
An official envoy asked him:
The Venerable Deshan Yuan was reviled by an old woman who said,
"Xuedou shook out his bowels of excrement to preach Chan for you."
That you could be so ungrateful and betray such kindness!
This was something Master Yunju Shun constantly criticized.
Chan Master Tianyi Huai was known for teaching "entanglement Chan" (ge-teng chan).
One day, upon hearing that Huai had passed away,
he joined his palms in the Dharma Hall and said:
Furthermore, it is a joy that the entangling vine-stump has been toppled.
Xiu Yuan-tong was at that time serving as the Rector (Vina) within the assembly;
he saw [the Master] incessantly scolding and reviling him.
He then said to his colleagues,
"I must settle this with that old fellow.
When the night assembly arrived, he again reviled him as before.
Xiu rose above the crowd and said in a stern voice,
"Have you not seen what is taught in the *Nirvana Sutra*?
Shun suddenly replied:
"I have stood for a long time before this great assembly; I trust you all remain in good health.
Having said this, he returned to his quarters.
Xiu remarked, "This old fellow has eyes all over his body."
He even rebuked Master Huai.
Xia Jingchun of Hunan was a man of talent and learning;
he once composed an inscription for the "Seamless Pagoda."
Chan Master Datong Ben used these words to answer the "Sutureless Pagoda" koan, saying:
"Mist and clouds arise upon its front and back."
The stars and moon circled the eaves and pillars.
Chūn resided at Yuelu Temple,
disciplining himself with diligent vigor.
Once, while walking up and down the palace steps at night, he lost his footing and fell.
A nearby monk helped him up,
but he remained dazed and unconscious, unable to attend to anything.
As for the writings he produced throughout his life,
even Chan Master Daoshao of Tuṣita could not understand them.
When he first traveled abroad and passed by Mount Lu,
he heard an elderly master speak of the matter of Chun;
Zhao was startled and said:
"In this life, my practice of Chan has not clarified the mind-ground, and I am just like Chun.
If even when I momentarily stumble I am still like this,
how much more so will it be after passing through the veil of death?"
When Grand Chancellor Lü Dàshēn was presiding over the government,
he took advantage of a day of rest from official duties to prepare a written petition requesting that a Lotus Sūtra fasting ritual be held.
The next day, he indeed arrived at the nobleman’s residence and sat upon the hall.
As Minister Shin was about to go out to see him,
he thought to himself:
If one bows, it is correct;
if one does not bow, it is incorrect.
Thus he spoke, calling out loudly:
Lü Laozi, you like such commotion;
come out quickly! Whether you prostrate yourself or not is up to you.
It was also well that he did not bow.
Shengong bowed to show his respect.
When the fast was completed, he asked whether the future would be auspicious or not.
He said, "I will ask for a brush and write the two characters 'Bozhou' (Boling) in large script and give them to you," without explaining his reason. Later,
after he had resigned from his post, while he was serving as the Governor of Bozhou and was arranging documents, [he found the inscription].
Suddenly, he saw two characters appearing before him;
only then did he realize that they were the previous prophecy.
Thus, Master Zhenjing retired from Dongshan.
While traveling through Zhejiang, he arrived at the monastery of Master Langlang Qi in Chuzhou.
At the request of the assembly, he gave a small-scale discourse (*xiao-can*),
wherein Zhenjing subjected the divergent views and heterodox interpretations of various quarters to critical scrutiny and refutation.
Without any sense of restraint,
a junior monk saw the Abbot rise from his seat and said,
"The Head of the Hall is here; fortunately, there is no other significant talk."
Qiyun said, "So it is! So it is!
The two looked at each other, laughed loudly, and departed.
The monk Xiangsheng of Yechuan was stern and austere;
the monastics revered him.
When Fushan Yuan and Tiantai Huai were among the assembly, [they encountered him].
I went specifically to seek his instruction;
it happened to be a time of snowy cold,
and he rebuked me and drove me away.
He went so far as to splash water on Dan-guo,
soaking all of his clothes;
the other monks were all incensed and departed.
Dharmika Wei-yuan gathered his bedding together, adjusted his robes,
and sat once more within the guest quarters.
Xianqing went to visit him and reproached him, saying:
"If you do not leave, I shall beat you.
Yuan Jin stepped forward and said,
"We two have come from thousands of li away."
I have come specifically to study the Chan of the Master;
how could I leave merely because you splashed me with a ladle of water?
Even if you were to beat me to death, I would not go.
The Provincial Governor laughed and said,
"You two wish to practice Chan,
yet you go to register as temporary residents."
He was subsequently requested to serve as the *karmadāna* (chief cook) at Yuan;
the community found his austere lifestyle difficult to endure. Once, while on an inspection tour of the manor, Xing happened to go out.
Yuan stealthily took the key to fetch oil and noodles to make a five-flavor porridge.
When the porridge was ready, he returned in haste to attend the hall.
After the meal, while sitting outside the hall, he ordered the invitation of the kitchen steward (diànzuò).
Yuanzhi said at the outset:
"I have indeed taken oil and flour to cook porridge;
I humbly wish to request that the Venerable Master punish me."
The provincial magistrate’s office completed the direct appraisal of his robes and bowl;
he was struck with thirty blows of the staff and expelled from the monastery,
to dwell far away in the marketplace.
He entrusted his case to a fellow practitioner to seek exoneration,
but Xing did not grant permission.
He spoke again, saying:
If there was no room for him to return home,
he simply requested to enter the hall with the assembly,
but this too was not granted.
One day, while out walking in the street,
he saw Yuan standing alone in front of an inn and said to him:
This is the gatehouse and corridor of the monastery.
You have stayed here for a long time;
have you ever returned the rent?
He had the amount owed calculated and pursued for collection;
without showing any sign of distress at the distance involved,
he took his alms bowl to the market to beg for money to repay it.
One day, while out on the street, Xingzhou saw him again.
Carrying his alms bowl back, he said to the assembly,
"Yuanzhen truly has the intention to practice Chan."
He then summoned him back.
One day, Chan Master Wude of Fenyang said to the assembly:
Last night, I dreamed that my deceased parents were seeking wine, meat, and paper money.
Unable to avoid conforming to worldly custom, I have prepared these offerings to sacrifice for them.
The ritual affairs were conducted in the storehouse hall.
Seating was arranged according to the customs of the secular world.
After the wine was served, the meat was distributed, and the paper money was burned.
He ordered the administrative officers and heads to gather the remaining trays and disperse them;
however, the officers refused to do so.
Without virtue, he sat alone at the banquet, eating and drinking as if nothing were amiss.
The assembly of monks said:
"How can monks who consume wine and meat be worthy of serving as teachers of the Dharma?"
His belongings were all taken away, leaving only six or seven people, including Ciming, Dayu, Quan, Daodao, and others.
On the following day, Wude ascended the hall and said:
Many idle gods and wild ghosts can be sent off with nothing more than a platter of wine and meat, along with two bundles of spirit-money.
As the *Lotus Sūtra* says:
This assembly has no branches or leaves;
it consists only of those who are steadfast and genuine. [The assembly] takes their seats.
When Master Zhenjing was traveling to visit various teachers,
he was walking along with two monks when they arrived at Guyin.
Daitou Bie asked him:
"When three people travel together, there is bound to be one who possesses wisdom. What is this one wisdom?
The two monks were speechless.
Jingli lowered his shoulders;
Yingsheng immediately let out a shout.
Bei clenched his fists and assumed a wrestling stance.
Jingyun said,
"There is no need for further examination.
Xue dragged his staff and drove him out.
Xue met Chan Master Cizhao of Shimen and Chan Master Fu of Yunding Mountain.
The Military Governor of Chengdu Prefecture invited him to ascend the seat within the government offices.
At that time, there was a commander of the music corps who came out to pay his respects;
rising, he looked back toward the mounting platform at the front of the street and said:
“I do not ask about ‘drinking up the waters of the West River in a single gulp.
For now, I request that you, Master, swallow the horse-landing platform before the street.
The Master extended both hands and sang:
Polish this thoroughly;
Master Yueying will surely gain realization through it.
This was written by Zangzhu Ziqing.
A native of Shu,
he was renowned throughout the monastic forests.
He traveled extensively to study under various great masters, including Zhenru, Haitang, and Pujué.
Having traveled to Mount Lu and entered the capital,
he met Chan Master Fayun Yuancong, who was traveling together with Master Xiu. Upon arriving at Fayun’s monastery,
Xiu was granted access to the meditation hall.
He sent for the abbot Qingzang to inform Yuantong.
Yuantong said,
"For now, have him lodge elsewhere."
I shall have him attend the hall as soon as a unit here becomes vacant.
Qingshan was at Zhikai when he happened to fall ill.
Xiu wished to go and inquire about his illness,
but as there were no visitors' passes at the mountain gate,
he secretly departed to see Jiqing at Zhihai.
Qing wrote a letter to Yuantong,
stating that Daoxiu’s conduct transcended conventional norms in both his public and private life.
Upon receiving the letter, Yuantong came to know of this.
At the night assembly, he cursed you vehemently;
this man is truly base.
It was out of a sense of righteousness that he risked being expelled from the monastery to come and inquire after your illness.
To instead report this as a malicious accusation—
how could such an act be performed by an upright person or a man of integrity?
Upon hearing this, Qing immediately suppressed his [anger] and ceased [the pursuit].
The entire monastic community said that [Yunmen] met his end after being rebuked once by Yuancong.
This was Master Mingshui Sun of Fuzhou.
While [the author] was serving as the attendant in the Dharma Cloud (Fayun) quarters,
Chan Master Daolin Lin arrived for lodging;
the Abbot specifically prepared tea for this new arrival.
Xun went to the official residence to invite him,
but just then Huilin was not present.
There was a fellow practitioner sitting at the same table as Huilin who said:
"Go and wait for him to come;
I shall request [an audience] for you.
Xun departed.
The monk forgot about it.
After the midday meal, the drum was struck to assemble for tea,
but Lin did not arrive.
Yuantong asked, "Is the newly arrived one here?
He then requested him to come forward.
When Lin arrived,
Yuantong ordered him to withdraw to sit on a couch and stand before the assembly,
reprimanding him, saying:
The Mountain Gate specially prepares tea to manifest the formal etiquette of the monastic community;
for what reason have you been negligent and failed to arrive at the appointed time?
Lín said, "Just now I heard the sound of drums;
suddenly, I feel an inner pressure."
As he hurried forward but could not advance,
Yuan Tong scolded him, saying,
"My drum is not a croton seed."
As soon as he struck it, excrement came out.
Xun stepped forward and said,
"It was I who forgot to request this."
"I am about to leave the monastery.
At that time, a fellow practitioner stepped forward from the assembly and said,
"This has nothing to do with the attendant or the newly arrived monk."
"It was not appropriate for me to accept this.
I forgot to request it on his behalf;
I shall now discharge both individuals from their obligations."
Yuantong admired his integrity and magnanimity,
and granted him clemency.
When the venerable masters of various quarters passed away, [he continued to honor them].
When his entire body was cremated, a great quantity of śarīra was obtained;
however, the śarīra of Master Zhennjing alone were as large as soybeans,
five-colored, crystalline, and exceedingly hard.
Zen Master Guzhan of Guyang was a preeminent disciple of Zhenjing;
he maintained a great deal of self-restraint.
He placed it in a lapis lazuli bottle and carried it with him for worship. Later,
Miaoxi traveled to Guyan Mountain.
He tested it by placing it upon an iron anvil and striking it with a hammer;
both the anvil and the hammer were indented.
Yet the śarīra remained undiminished.
Is this not the result of his lifelong practice,
his clear realization of the Path, and his transcendent attainment?
Xian Pengtou was a native of Jiangzhou.
He was a preeminent figure among the disciples of Venerable Zhenru of Mount Wei.
His realization was clear and his spiritual acuity was sharp;
he possessed works that surpassed those of his teacher.
However, his conduct was not disciplined.
The assembly unanimously agreed to this.
Zhēnrú then constructed a small hermitage behind the abbot’s quarters and had Xián dwell there alone.
Only a narrow path was permitted to pass directly in front of the abbot’s quarters;
it was not allowed for brothers to come and go there.
Two years later.
When he raises his head before the assembly and stands as a monk to wield the whisk and preach the Dharma,
there is a quality that greatly surpasses that of ordinary men.
The entire assembly changed their views because of this.
Later, he went to Xingyang in Yingzhou,
where for several years his Way flourished greatly.
He entered nirvana;
his physical body remained incorruptible.
Master Yuanwu witnessed this event while at Mount Guiyang.
When Miaoxi traveled to Xingyang,
he was still able to see the physical body of Master Zhantang Zun.
A native of Xingyuan Prefecture,
he was the direct successor of Zhenjing.
When the seat of Yunyan in Fenning was vacant, [he was invited to fill it].
The Prefectural Governor commanded Chan Master Hwangnyong Sisin to nominate someone he knew well to fill that position.
Sishin said, "Zhun has succeeded in maintaining the mountain monastery;
I do not know him."
He remarked, "I have only seen the 'Verses on Washing the Alms Bowl,' which is truly excellent.
The Prefect asked, "May I hear it?"
Sishin raised [the topic] and said:
"Zhi-hu-ye-zhe— this is the nostrils of a patch-robed monk."
The great head is turned downward.
If you still do not understand,
go ask Old Lady Wang of the Eastern Village.
The governor and the prefect marveled at him.
They prepared the full ceremonial rites and earnestly invited him; Zhun did not decline.
Throughout his life, he regulated himself with frugality;
even while leading disciples and propagating the Dharma,
he did not alter his conduct from when he was among the monastic community.
After rising at dawn,
one should go to the washstand and take only a small ladle of hot water to wash the face;
then, use it again to wash the feet.
Other forms of communal enjoyment were all of this nature.
As soon as the formal session had concluded, [the master] said:
The abbot’s attendant and laborers were treated like ordinary travelers;
he personally performed tasks such as sweeping the floor and brewing tea,
possessing the refined bearing of an ancient master.
This is a true model for future generations.
Chan Master Fayun Foguo Zhaogao once retired to the Iron Arhat Hall at Jingde Temple.
In the hall there were several wooden arhats;
as the capital was suffering from bitter cold,
Hui-gao took them and burned them.
He sat by the brazier until dawn.
On the following day, he retrieved countless *śarīra* relics from within the ashes.
The various masters of the seats [were amazed].
All regarded him as a follower of external paths;
yet Fozhao was actually of the same lineage as Danxia—
something that cannot be verified by the eyes of the mundane.
Chen Liaoweng of Yanping,
whose given name was Guan and courtesy name Yingzhong.
He styled himself the "Huayan Layman.
He was upright and incorruptible in court,
possessing the dignified spirit of the ancients.
He applied himself with focused attention to the inner scriptures (Buddhist texts), and his debates were so compelling that he could displace others from their seats;
yet, he alone had not yet achieved a great awakening through the practice of Chan.
The Chan school’s *nidānas* are mostly understood through mental interpretation;
he was a fervent admirer of Master Nanshan’s recorded sayings,
having provided exhaustive commentaries upon them.
Only Vajra rubbed the back of the clay figure;
the commentary states that this was not to be practiced.
He once said to people:
This must certainly have its source;
however, there is as yet no one who knows it.
As the proverb says:
"Before a person of great wisdom, there is a darkness three feet deep.
This is indeed not false.
Thus it was said by Chan Master Cizhao Cong.
A descendant of Shoushan,
he resided at Shimen in Xiangzhou during the Xuancheng era.
One day, the local governor, acting on personal animosity, flogged and humiliated him.
Upon his arrival, the assembly of monks welcomed him from the left side of the road.
The head seat hurried forward to inquire after him, saying,
"The Prefect has unjustly subjected the Master to such humiliation."
Jizhao pointed to the ground with his finger and said,
"A pile of bones rises from level ground.
As he pointed, a mound of earth surged up.
When the Prefect heard of this,
he ordered someone to scrape it away;
yet it surged forth again as before.
Later, the Prefect’s entire family died in Xiangzhou.
Furthermore, a monk asked:
"In the midst of deep mountains and rocky cliffs..."
"Furthermore, is there also the Buddha-dharma or not?
Zhao said, "There is.
[The student] further asked:
"What is the Buddha-dharma within the deep mountains and rocky precipices? Zhao said,
"A strange stone, its shape resembling a tiger."
"When fire burns the pine trees, its power is like a dragon.
Master Wujin loved these words,
yet the *Shimen Lu* alone does not record these two matters.
All of this was personally witnessed by Miaoxi and recounted by the Layman Wujin.
Recorded by Li Shanglao of Mount Lu.
Because he had disturbed the earth by carrying out construction work,
the entire family fell ill with swellings;
they sought medical treatment, but to no avail.
Thereupon, he thoroughly swept the chambers and quarters,
commanded his kinsmen to each purify their minds,
burned incense, and recited the *Chishengguang* (Blazing Radiance) mantra.
He performed incantations to appease the offended spirits.
Before seven days had passed,
he dreamed at night.
An elderly man dressed in white robes was riding an ox at his home when,
suddenly, the ground beneath him sank and he disappeared as the earth spun away.
On the following day, everyone— both great and small— was found to be unharmed.
What is moved by sincere resolve is as swift as a shadow following a form or an echo responding to a sound;
could it be that the Buddha’s power is not capable of such a thing?
Yong was the son of Chan Master Yuanzhao Ben;
he attained awakening as a result of falling down.
He composed a verse, saying:
"This one encounter, this one encounter—
ten thousand taels of gold would be worth it."
A hat upon his head and a bundle at his waist;
he carries the clear breeze and the bright moon upon the tip of his staff.
When Lord Zheng of Fu frequently attended court audiences, he would inquire about this.
One day, while observing the Master ascending the hall and looking about him to left and right, he suddenly attained awakening.
He sent a verse to Yuanzhao, saying:
"Upon seeing Master Yong once, my realization entered deeply."
Through causes and conditions, I have inherited the mind of my teacher;
though mountains and rivers lie a thousand miles apart, they are not separated by clouds.
Facing the numinous light and the wondrous sound before my very eyes.
When Zheng Gong retired from the相位 (prime ministership) and resided in Luocheng,
he longed for Yong’s instruction and requested that he stay at the monastery.
Upon hearing that [Wang] Yong had entered the border, [Wang Anshi] personally went out to meet him.
Just as they were about to mount the carriage, Sima Guang arrived.
He asked, "Where is the Excellency going?
Zheng Gong replied,
"To receive Chan Master Yongyong of Zhaoti."
Lord Wen said,
"I shall go with you as well.
They then rode side by side out of the city walls.
He waited at the postal station for a long time.
Suddenly, he saw dozens of loads passing by.
Master Wen asked, "Whose luggage is that?"
The bearer replied, "This is the baggage of Master Xin Zhaoti. Thereupon,
Master Wen took his horse and returned.
Duke Zheng said,
"I intended to see the Avataṃsaka Sūtra;
for what reason have you returned first?"
Wen Gong said, "I have already seen him.
He eventually returned first to Miaoxi; this was once told by Li Yizhong, the Vice Minister.
Shun Laofu resided at Qixian on Mount Lu,
while Huai Dugu served as the Magistrate of Nankang;
due to a private grievance, he stripped him of his robes.
The Chan Master Liai of Jingyin Dajue once entered the chamber of Emperor Shun and heard that Shun had returned to secular life.
He sent someone to fetch [the image] back to Jingyin Temple;
he yielded his main quarters to it for residence and occupied a side chamber himself.
Emperor Renzong summoned Liàn several times to enter the inner palace and inquire about the Way,
yet he ultimately did not speak of the matter concerning Shun.
One day, Prince Jia received an imperial decree to provide a meal for the monastic community at Jingyin Monastery.
There he saw Dajue standing by Emperor Shun’s side with great reverence.
He returned to report this to Emperor Renzong.
The Emperor summoned him for an audience in the private chamber;
upon seeing him, he sighed and said:
The resonance of his Way was extraordinary and magnificent.
A true mountain-dwelling man of refined character,
he inscribed upon a fan:
Xiaoshun was granted permission to remain as a monk;
by special imperial decree, he was once again appointed to reside at Qixian Temple,
and was further bestowed with purple robes and a silver alms bowl.
On the day Emperor Shun ceased his practice of living as a hermit among the worthy,
two men of great strength carried his sedan chair to the front of Luohan Temple.
The two of them said to one another,
"Since he is not the elder of our monastery,
we cannot go far."
He abandoned his palanquin and returned.
When Shun arrived again,
he sent someone ahead to comfort and reassure the two laborers, saying:
What you did at that time was correct;
simply set your mind at ease and need not harbor doubt or fear.
Shun entered the hall and ascended the seat, offering this verse:
Unjustly slandered and falsely accused,
I suffered misfortune for more than half a year as a layman;
today, I have returned once more to Sanxia Temple.
"How much joy? How much anger?
One day, Master Shunlao raised this point.
Abbot Yanguan called to his attendant.
"Bring the rhinoceros fan.
The attendant said,
"The fan has already been broken."
The Official said:
"Since the fan is broken,
give me back the rhinoceros."
The attendant had no reply. Shun said,
"At this time of the three months of summer heat, one truly needs a fan."
Acting as an attendant, he failed to understand the matter. Nevertheless,
Yanguan was far too prolix.
"Why do you not all simply let go?
If the attendant had seen Yan-guan say, 'The fan is already broken; now return me my rhinoceros,' he would have immediately replied:"
It has already been cast onto the heap of refuse.
Cuiyan Zhen Dianxiong once reviled Master Shun Lao for preaching "Zen of non-action."
Master Shishuang Yong sent someone to deliver a message to Zhen, saying:
"Shun’s realization of the 'ancient mirror' at Dongshan was based on such an occasion;
how could this possibly be called 'Chan of non-action'?"
"You scolded him, and you yourself lost one eye. When Shun heard this, he composed a verse, saying:
"Yunju does not understand Chan."
Having washed one's feet, one goes to bed to sleep.
The winter melon is straight and blunt;
the bottle gourd is curved and winding.
Master Yong also composed a verse, saying:
"Shishuang does not understand Zen;
he washes his feet and goes up to bed to sleep."
The pillow fell to the ground,
smashing the monastery brick.
One day, Shun ascended the hall and said:
After dusk, he removed his robes and slept.
Rising at dawn, he immediately prepared his traveling pack.
Last night the wind blew and the fence fell down.
He called for his servants to split bamboo rafts and bind them back up.
He then descended from his seat.
In the assembly of the Fifth Patriarch, there was a monk named Fahai.
During his entry into the inner room, the Patriarch asked him:
"He who does not take the myriad dharmas as his companion—"
"Who is it? The monk replied, "It is Fatao. [The Master] said, "That is not so."
The Patriarch pointed with his finger and said, "Stop, stop! Fali, it is not so; how is it?
At these words, Fali attained realization.
Later, he went to the quarters of Master Xuānmìduó at Dōnglín, where he fully attained the essence of the "plain and real" (píngshí) teaching.
One day, Fǎzàng took a single branch of flowers,
circumambulated the meditation seat once, and [placed them before the Master].
Placing his hands behind his back and inserting them into the incense burner,
he said, "Preceptor, tell me:
what is your intention?"
